title: Stefan Kainbacher. Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1. Decode
location:
Kunstraum Engländerbau (Lageplan)
Städtle 37
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
An expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode is an expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

In the center of the art space are eight black 19-inch server racks, arranged in a circle like a technological Stonehenge. The racks form the habitat of a hybrid organism in which plants, sensors, computers, artificial intelligence and audiovisual systems are connected.

Each rack houses live plants, full-spectrum grow lights, speakers, and various technical components. Network cables, power lines and hoses of an automated irrigation system connect the individual units into a common circuit. The technical infrastructure deliberately remains visible and becomes part of the spatial composition.

The plants are continuously recorded using various sensors. The focus is on measuring bioelectrical signals using Plant SpikerBox systems, supplemented by environmental and climate data. Four of the experimental stations also have camera systems with which the plants can be visually observed.

The collected data is processed by a locally operated multi-agent system. The AI ​​agents analyze electrical activity patterns, image data and environmental parameters and try to recognize connections, states and recurring patterns in the behavior of the plants. The installation stages this process not as a solved problem, but as an ongoing attempt at a machine approach to a non-human form of communication.

The work is seen as an artistic research setting: The AI ​​does not try to control plants, but rather to understand them. The actual topic of the work is less the plant itself and more the question of how technical systems create meaning and what limits exist.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode marks the first part of an ongoing series of works. While this chapter addresses the question of decoding biological signals, future chapters will examine additional forms of interaction, translation, and coexistence between human and non-human actors.

title: State holiday - host community
description:
Host community on the national holiday 2026: We invite you to celebrate
On August 15, 2026, our community will be dedicated to the Liechtenstein state holiday. After mass in Bendern Church and the official state ceremony in Vaduz, visitors can look forward to a colorful festival program for the whole family from midday on Peter-Kaiser-Platz.
The Liechtenstein national holiday will be a special occasion for our community. As a host community, we actively participate in the celebrations and warmly invite the population and guests to experience this traditional holiday together.
The day begins at 8 a.m. with the solemn mass in Bendern Church. The musical accompaniment is provided exclusively by the organ. The service ends at around 8:45 a.m. before the participants set off together to Vaduz at 9 a.m. The official state ceremony begins there at 10:30 a.m. Tickets are required to attend the state ceremony. The ticket contingent at the municipality of Gamprin has already been exhausted. Further information on this can be found at staatsferientag.li.
From 12 p.m., Peter-Kaiser-Platz will be transformed into a lively meeting place for young and old. Six clubs from the community are looking forward to welcoming visitors: the volunteer fire department, the boy scouts, the ski club, the Gampriner Buschmönschterle, the Konkordia music club and the BIZLadies. Together, the clubs ensure a varied culinary offering of food and drinks.
The entertainment program also promises a varied afternoon. A bouncy castle and adhesive tattoos are available for children and families. The festival is complemented by a special stage program put together by the cultural commission.
With the diverse offering, Gamprin wants to make the national holiday a sociable and connecting experience for the entire community.

title: Finissage | In the context of the collection: RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
location:
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Lageplan)
Städtle 32
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
Guided tour and conversation with Christiane Meyer-Stoll and RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
In cooperation with the Liechtenstein Art Society.

Marie-Antoinette Chiarenza (born 1957 in Tunis, TN) and Daniel Hauser (born 1959 in Bern, CH) have been working together since 1983 - since 1997 under the programmatic name RELAX.
The name stands for an attitude that suspends speed, pressure of expectation and tension and creates space for reflection and fundamental questions.

RELAX mostly work situation-related and take into account both the exhibition location and social, political, economic and ecological contexts. Her multimedia works question social values ​​as well as the canon and structures of art. With fine humor and an inquiring eye, RELAX opens up new perspectives: your room installation What is wealth? (2010–2017) from the collection of the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein forms the starting point for further thoughts about value, possession, responsibility, memory - and happiness.

Works by RELAX have already given the title to exhibitions at the museum twice: Who pays? (2006) 2017 and What do we want to keep? (2018) 2021. With such open questions or groundbreaking statements, RELAX calls for thinking together - because thinking alone is criminal.

The exhibition What is wealth? was created in close collaboration with RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co). She combines her works from the collection with a series of works created specifically for this solo presentation.

A production by the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, curated by Christiane Meyer-Stoll with Leslie Ospelt.

description:
Time out with culture!

Make your lunch break a time out with culture! Experience an inspiring 30-minute tour with the artist Ursula Wolf through our special exhibition “What was important today” and then enjoy a delicious soup.

For ten years, the Liechtenstein artist Ursula Wolf drew for media coverage every day. What started as a drawing exercise soon became a large collection of small works of art. They document what moved the artist herself, but also Liechtenstein and the world during these ten years. It also talks about the value we attach to events, how fleeting this evaluation can be and how surprisingly long-lasting seemingly trivial things sometimes remain.
 
Ursula Wolf presents these drawings in the Liechtenstein State Museum in the form of a walk-in collage: a space that invites you to discover, think and often smile.

title: Finissage | In the context of the collection: RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
location:
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Lageplan)
Städtle 32
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
Guided tour and conversation with Christiane Meyer-Stoll and RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
In cooperation with the Liechtenstein Art Society.

Marie-Antoinette Chiarenza (born 1957 in Tunis, TN) and Daniel Hauser (born 1959 in Bern, CH) have been working together since 1983 - since 1997 under the programmatic name RELAX.
The name stands for an attitude that suspends speed, pressure of expectation and tension and creates space for reflection and fundamental questions.

RELAX mostly work situation-related and take into account both the exhibition location and social, political, economic and ecological contexts. Her multimedia works question social values ​​as well as the canon and structures of art. With fine humor and an inquiring eye, RELAX opens up new perspectives: your room installation What is wealth? (2010–2017) from the collection of the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein forms the starting point for further thoughts about value, possession, responsibility, memory - and happiness.

Works by RELAX have already given the title to exhibitions at the museum twice: Who pays? (2006) 2017 and What do we want to keep? (2018) 2021. With such open questions or groundbreaking statements, RELAX calls for thinking together - because thinking alone is criminal.

The exhibition What is wealth? was created in close collaboration with RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co). She combines her works from the collection with a series of works created specifically for this solo presentation.

A production by the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, curated by Christiane Meyer-Stoll with Leslie Ospelt.

Humorous, surprising and touching - that is the company Tarkabarka from Liechtenstein. For 10 years, Anna and Bálint Kostyál-Büchel have been chugging through Switzerland, Liechtenstein, southern Germany, Austria and Hungary with their nostalgic circus wagon team. Her two children and her circus dog Buksi are always there.

The Tarkabarka company delights with expressive theater, fine clowning, fast acrobatics and poetic moments and lets children and adults alike forget time in front of the backdrop of the circus wagon. In her two pieces “KABUFF” and “HOPPAA!!” tell a lot - without words! Come in!

title: Festival Vaduz Classic «After Work Concert» Pure Percussion
description:
Pulsating rhythms, quick-witted virtuosity and sophisticated sounds: a concert for everyone who wants to leave everyday life behind them in a relaxed atmosphere after work.

Anyone who thinks of timpani and snare drums when they hear the term percussion will definitely be surprised this evening: the focus is on the marimba - an instrument with an expressive power that can best be described as voluminous resonance in all registers. At this after work concert, Christoph Sietzen and Bogdan Bacanu take the audience right into the heart of pulsating rhythms, quick-witted virtuosity and sophisticated sounds. The two artists have been making music together for many years. What they have in common is not only exceptional technical precision, but above all their playful lightness and great stage presence. “Pure Percussion” is a concert for the curious – for lovers of classical music as well as for everyone who wants to leave everyday life behind them in a relaxed atmosphere after work.

location:

description:
Take a seat, lean back and enjoy the most beautiful melodies of opera literature right in the heart of Liechtenstein.

On this summer evening, the Vaduz town hall square is transformed into an open-air opera stage - with a backdrop that no set designer in the world could create. Because as soon as the sun slowly disappears behind the mountains and the first notes sound, the music unfolds its very special magic. Two of the most important opera stars of our time contribute to this: the soprano Nadine Sierra and the tenor Javier Camarena, who delight audiences at the world's major opera houses. After joint successes in Verdi's "La traviata" and Gounod's "Roméo et Juliette", they can now be experienced for the first time at VADUZ CLASSIC and give us an unforgettable evening with arias and duets full of passion, virtuosity and emotions. Look forward to a concert that touches, thrills and resonates for a long time. And if you shed a tear or two of emotion, you're in good company.

title: Festival Vaduz Classic “Masterpieces” Gautier Capuçon & Ensemble Capucelli
location:
Vaduzer Saal (Lageplan)
Giessenstrasse 7
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
This evening's musical menu includes French sophistication, Italian passion and a touch of Argentine melancholy.

A good menu does not depend on a single course, but on the successful composition. It surprises, arouses curiosity and unfolds its charm from aisle to aisle. It's the same with this concert. The Ensemble Capucelli serves a little bit of everything – although not on plates, but with seven cellos. With Gautier Capuçon and the Ensemble Capucelli, seven outstanding cellists will be on stage. The ensemble was created through Capuçon's commitment to promoting young talent and brings together former award winners of his support program. Together, the seven cellists develop an ensemble sound that is as homogeneous as it is colorful and impressively show how versatile the cello is - as a solo instrument, as a chamber music partner and as a sound body of almost orchestral fullness. Rossini's "William Tell", Tchaikovsky's "Waltz of the Flowers", Ravel's "Boléro" or Piazzolla's "La muerte del ángel" are heard in arrangements specially created for cello ensembles and open up new perspectives on well-known masterpieces. A concert full of sonic discoveries: varied, surprising and with a pinch of French elegance.

title: Festival Vaduz Classic “Classic meets Electro” with Catching Flies
location:
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Lageplan)
Café
Städtle 32
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
Catching Flies is a British multi-instrumentalist and DJ. With synthesizers and a string quartet, he transforms the café in the art museum into a mixture of nightclub and concert hall.

Behind the name “Catching Flies” is the British multi-instrumentalist, producer and DJ George King. His music moves effortlessly between electronic beats and acoustic sound worlds. Warm synthesizer sounds meet strings, finely interwoven rhythms meet catchy melodies. “Catching Flies” is known for its unmistakably warm and atmospheric sound. His tracks combine atmospheric electronics with complex rhythms and range from hip-hop to house to soul and jazz. Together with his British string quartet, he transforms the CAFE in the art museum into a mixture of urban nightclub and stylish concert hall. “Catching Flies” has impressively proven in recent years that this connection is much more than an exciting experiment. His recent highlights include a BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix, a live video with the string quartet for Anjunadeep, one of the most famous electronic music labels in the world, and a live performance of his track “Orsay” at the Musée d’Orsay in Paris. A concert to listen to, immerse yourself in and take part in: atmospherically dense and sonically sophisticated – the perfect soundtrack for a long festival night.
